nodes.text: Each role, its quarter and its why, the funnel math from sourcing to signed, the process with time targets, the risks, and what we need from you.
Dana Whitfield, Head of People  ·  1 December 2026
hold us to every date in here
Each role, its quarter, and its why
the Q1 column is the one to argue with
of the sourced pass the screen
The two-hour panel, in one day
of screens go on to a panel
of panels end in an offer
Seven days from offer to ink
Bars on a square-root scale so the bottom stays readable. The counts are the plan for the half; the rates are last year's, with the accept rate held at 85%.
at a 15% screen we would need 1,470 names
Four stages, each with an owner and a clock. The funnel math only holds if every clock does.
a panel in one day, never across a week
Recruiter, 30 minutes, within five days of applying. Owner: Talent.
Two hours in one day, never across a week. Owner: hiring manager.
Debrief within 24 hours, offer or no within 48. Owner: hiring manager.
Offer to signature in seven days; a call from the exec sponsor for every senior role. Owner: People.
the 48-hour decision is the one we break most
Who is on the hook for what
Owns the close: every offer out within 48 hours, signed within seven days.
Owns the ten engineering roles and the panel that runs in one day.
Owns the six territory hires and the enterprise pod, staffed by March.
Owns the three pod hires and the interviewer hours from her leads.
if a date slips, one of these four says so first
Comp bands, competing offers, and timing
Engineering bands are 8% under the latest survey. Ask: adjust in January, not after the first lost offer.
Two competing offers per senior role
Every platform candidate is talking to two others. Mitigation: seven-day close, and the sponsor call.
Q1 starts in the quiet weeks
Nobody changes jobs in early January. Sourcing starts in December or Q1 slips.
the band fix costs less than one lost offer
Referrals for the six platform roles, four hours a week of interviewer time from every team lead, and the band adjustment approved in January.
the first six names are the hard ones
